one_liner: OpenCL non-local means denoiser plugin for AviSynth(+) and VapourSynth; one user anecdote shows it about 2.5-3x faster than HandBrake's CPU NLMeans.
what_it_does: Spatio-temporal NLMeans video denoiser that runs on any OpenCL 1.2 GPU or CPU device. It ships as a frame-server plugin, KNLMeansCL(clip, d, a, s, h, channels, wmode, wref, rclip, device_type, device_id, ...) in AviSynth/AviSynth+ and core.knlm.KNLMeansCL in VapourSynth; d is the temporal radius, a the search radius, s the patch radius, h the strength. It is not a library API and not an FFmpeg or HandBrake filter, so it does not drop in for the baseline; its parameters do not map one to one onto HandBrake NLMeans settings.
how_it_is_fast: Implements the Goossens et al. (ACIVS 2010) GPU NLMeans scheme: for each search offset q it builds a per-pixel squared-difference image (nlmDistance), box-filters it into patch distances with separable horizontal and vertical kernels that tile through __local memory (O(s) per pixel per pass instead of O(s^2)), turns them into weights (native_exp for the Welsch mode) and accumulates. Weights are symmetric, so only half the (2a+1)^2(2d+1) window is computed and each distance image serves both p+q and p-q. Frame size, radii and channel layout are baked into the kernel as -D constants at build time with -cl-fast-relaxed-math, and work-group shapes are picked per vendor from CL_DEVICE_MAX_WORK_GROUP_SIZE.
when_to_use: AviSynth+ or VapourSynth encode scripts that need NLMeans denoising and have an otherwise idle GPU while x264/x265 keep the CPU busy.
AMD or Intel GPUs where CUDA-only denoisers (for example BM3DCUDA) are not an option; OpenCL 1.2 covers AMD, Intel and NVIDIA.
Chroma-only or 4:2:0 denoising at 1080p: the wiki's RX 480 table shows the UV planes of 4:2:0 at up to 67 fps versus about 25 fps for 8-bit luma.
Workflows that compute weights on a prefiltered reference clip (rclip) and apply them to the original.
when_not_to_use: HandBrake- or FFmpeg-only pipelines: it is a frame-server plugin and cannot be loaded there (HandBrake issue 839 requesting it is closed); use FFmpeg nlmeans_opencl or av-denoise instead.
Apple Silicon or macOS AMD GPUs: issue 56 (flashing pink/green frames on M1, open since 2023-05-02) is only fixed in unmerged PR 60 (2026-04-10).

CPU-only machines: it needs an OpenCL CPU runtime (issues 51 and 57 report device_type='cpu' failures), and search snippets of the Doom9 thread (forum blocked here) put TNLMeans level with it on a weak CPU.
4:4:4, RGB or float clips at high resolution: the wiki table drops to about 9 fps at 1080p on an RX 480, and clips above 8192x8192 are refused.
Projects that need maintained binaries: the last tagged release is v1.1.1, master (1.1.1e) last changed on 2023-01-05, and issue 58 (2025-11-27) asks for a new build.

integration.dependencies: OpenCL 1.2 ICD and a vendor runtime; VapourSynth API 3 headers (VapourSynth.h, VSHelper.h) or AviSynth+ headers; meson.build also requires Boost filesystem/system although no source file includes Boost; Windows builds need the Visual C++ 2015 redistributable
integration.min_toolchain: C++11 (meson cpp_std=gnu++11), OpenCL 1.2 (0.6.11 is the last release for OpenCL 1.0/1.1)
integration.platforms: Windows, Linux, macOS; any OpenCL 1.2 GPU, CPU or accelerator (wiki lists AMD HD 5800+, Intel HD 2500+, NVIDIA GT 640+); maximum 8192x8192
integration.thread_safety: One command queue and one set of device buffers per filter instance; VapourSynth mode fmParallelRequests serialises frame processing per instance, AviSynth+ uses MT_MULTI_INSTANCE (one OpenCL context per thread). Building the kernel calls setlocale(LC_ALL, "C") then setlocale(LC_ALL, ""), which changes the whole process's locale (issue 43, open).

gotchas: Possible stale-frame bug at the end of a clip (from reading NLMVapoursynth.cpp and NLMAvisynth.cpp, not tested): uploads cover frames n+k_start..n+k_end with k_end clamped to the clip end, but the symmetric loop still reads the future slot t-k for every k down to k_start = -min(d, n). For the last d frames those slots hold whatever an earlier request uploaded. In strict sequential order that is the last frame repeated; under out-of-order requests (seeking, multithreaded vspipe) it is an unrelated frame, which would blend into the output.

Each output frame re-uploads all 2d+1 input frames, issues 4 to 7 kernel launches per search offset (about 37 offsets at the defaults a=2, d=1) and ends with a blocking clFinish, so there is no overlap of transfer and compute across frames; one instance per GPU stays single-stream.

Driver-specific breakage is fixed only in unmerged PRs: macOS buffer-fill sync (PR 60), Radeon compiler crash from unused nlmUnpack image arguments (PR 59), AUTO device fallback on runtimes that return CL_INVALID_VALUE (PR 61). Mesa OpenCL is not recognised (issue 55).

Manual ocl_x/ocl_y/ocl_r overrides are not checked against s: the horizontal and vertical kernels need block width and height of at least s, or their __local buffer reads go out of bounds (the auto-selected blocks are at least 8 and s is limited to 8).
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it over av-denoise when the pipeline is AviSynth+ or VapourSynth rather than FFmpeg and you need temporal NLMeans on a non-NVIDIA GPU; pick VapourSynth-BM3DCUDA instead when you have NVIDIA hardware and want BM3D quality, since KNLMeansCL publishes no head-to-head numbers against either.
verified_claims_summary: The only comparison is a 2017 HandBrake feature request (issue 839, CvH): about 17-20 fps whole-encode speed with HandBrake's built-in CPU NLMeans versus 50-55 fps with KNLMeansCL on the same file (about 2.5-3.2x), with no hardware, resolution, filter settings or versions. Because the issue asks HandBrake to add KNLMeansCL, the faster run cannot have been inside HandBrake, so the two numbers come from different, unstated pipelines. The wiki Benchmark page gives absolute fps only (v1.0.2, 1080p, d=1 a=2 s=4, Core i5-4690 with Radeon RX 480, Windows 10).
status_note: Abandoned upstream (last commit 2023-01-05, three driver-fix PRs from 2026-04-10 unmerged), GPL-3.0, so it is fine as a plugin but cannot be vendored into permissively licensed code; the pinterf fork carries later AviSynth+ work.
